chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the sacrifice of the castrated animal, and he said, 'There is no objection.'

key_terms.اَلْخَصِيِّ: The castrated animal (specifically referring to a male animal whose testicles have been removed)
key_terms.ذَبِيحَةِ: Sacrifice (the act of slaughtering an animal for food or ritual purposes)
key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ: There is no objection / It is permissible (a common legal phrase indicating permissibility without strong recommendation or prohibition)

ai.seo_question: Is the meat of a castrated animal permissible for sacrifice in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms the permissibility of consuming meat from a castrated animal, addressing a specific query regarding the ritual validity of such sacrifices. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that castration does not invalidate the animal's status as *halal* for consumption, provided other conditions of slaughter are met, distinguishing it from certain cultural taboos or specific prohibitions found in other schools of thought.
